text: From the categorical viewpoint, why is − ⊗_R M right exact?
choices: It is a left adjoint (to Hom_R(M, −)), and left adjoints preserve colimits, in particular cokernels
It is a right adjoint, and right adjoints preserve limits
Tensoring preserves injections for every module M
Because M can always be chosen free
explanation: The tensor–hom adjunction Hom(A ⊗ M, B) ≅ Hom(A, Hom(M, B)) makes − ⊗ M a left adjoint, and left adjoints preserve all colimits, hence cokernels and right exactness. Preservation of injections is precisely flatness, which fails in general (ℤ/nℤ over ℤ).
